The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council
with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically,
adjourned meetings are held on the last Friday of every month at 8:30 a.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the City Clerk via email at CityClerk@CityofSanMarino.org or by phone at
(626) 300­0705 prior to the meeting for assistance.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City will
do it’s best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

How to offer public comment from home:
  1. Public comment will be accepted by email to CityClerk@CityofSanMarino.org until 3:00
  p.m. the day before the meeting, to be read by the City Clerk during public comment.
  Lengthy public comment may be summarized in the interest of time, and previously
  distributed public comment will be noted. Any comments received after 3:00 p.m. will
  be included in the public comment record but will not be read at the meeting.
  2. Public comment will be accepted electronically via the zoom.us teleconference module
  during the meeting. Zoom comments will be taken after the in­person comments.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

Council Member Chou, Council Member Lo, Council Member Shepherd Romey, Vice Mayor
Huang, and Mayor Talt

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall,
2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the Stoneman
Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s website:
http://www.cityofsanmarino.org.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the City Council by
completing a public comment card and giving it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. At
this time, the public may address the City Council on items that are not on the agenda.
Pursuant to state law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on issues not on the
meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The Mayor reserves the right to place
limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow up on such items.

1.  ACCEPTANCE OF DONATION FROM THE HUNTINGTON LIBRARY, ART
  MUSEUM, AND BOTANICAL GARDENS OF $100,000 FOR RECEIPT IN
  THE CAPITAL PROJECTS FUND
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council accept the donation and apply
  the funds to capital projects, the appropriate motion would be: “I move to accept
  the donation of $100,000 from the Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical
  Gardens; authorize the Finance Department to receipt the donation in the Capital
  Projects Fund; and amend the FY 2022­23 revenue budget to recognize revenue of
  $100,000 in the Capital Projects Fund (Account # 394­00­3601­0000).”

2.  APPROVAL OF AN AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF SAN MARINO
  AND FLOCK SAFETY FOR A FIVE­YEAR SUBSCRIPTION IN AN
  AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $505,850
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve the Agreement
  between the City of San Marino and Flock Safety for a Five­Year Subscription. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be: “I
  move to approve the Agreement between the City of San Marino and Flock Safety
  for a Five­Year Subscription not to exceed $505,850, and authorize the City Manager
  to execute the agreement on behalf of the City.”

3.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. R­23­23 AMENDING THE
  UNREPRESENTED EMPLOYEES SALARY AND BENEFITS SCHEDULE
  AND RESOLUTION NO. R­23­24 UPDATING THE SALARY SCHEDULE
  FOR FY 2023­2024
  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. R­23­23, Resolution No.
  R­23­24, and direct Finance staff to increase each department’s operating budget in
  the necessary amount. If Council concurs, an appropriate motion would be: “I move
  to (1) adopt Resolution No. R­23­23, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
  San Marino, California, Amending the Unrepresented Employees Salary and Benefits
  Schedule for the Period Covering July 1, 2022 Through June 30, 2024 Pertaining to
  Police Chief Classification, Deletion of Human Resources Manager, and the Addition of
  Classifications of Code Enforcement Officer, Recreation Coordinator, and Police
  Records Clerk to the Part­Time Employees Salary Schedule; (2) adopt Resolution No.
  R­23­24, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of San Marino, California,
  Approving the Updated Salary Schedule for FY 2023­2024; and (3) approve
  additional appropriations in the amount of $25,695 in FY 2023­2024 to be spread
  over the affected full­time personnel budget line items as shown in the respective
  budgets.”

5.  ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. O­23­1402 (SECOND READING)
  ADDING ARTICLE 20 AND MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 23.02.34 TO
  MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 23 AND AMENDING MUNICIPAL CODE
  SECTION 23.03.10 REGARDING DEVELOPMENT STANDARDS AND
  OBJECTIVE DESIGN STANDARDS FOR MULTI­FAMILY RESIDENTIAL
  DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS IN THE C­1 ZONE
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council adopt Ordinance No. O­23­1402. If
  the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation an appropriate motion would
  be: “I move to waive full reading and adopt Ordinance No. O­23­1402, an Ordinance
  of the City Council of San Marino, California adding Article 20 and Municipal Code
  Section 23.02.34 to Municipal Code Chapter 23, and Amending 23.03.10 Regarding
  Development Standards and Objective Design Standards for Multi­Family Residential
  Development Projects.”

6.  ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. O­23­1403 (2ND READING)
  AMENDING MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 02.14.02 REMOVING
  LANGUAGE PERTAINING TO PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  ABSENCES AND RESOLUTION NO. R­23­16 ESTABLISHING
  ADVISORY BODY ATTENDANCE STANDARDS
  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends the Council adopt Ordinance No. O­23­1403 and Resolution No. R­
  23­16. If Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would
  be: “I move to waive full reading and adopt by title only Ordinance No. O­23­1403,
  an Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Marino, California Amending
  Municipal Code Section 02.14.02 Removing Language Pertaining to Public Safety
  Commission Absences, and Resolution No. O­23­16, a Resolution of the City Council
  of the City of San Marino, Establishing Advisory Body Attendance Standards.”

7.  AUTHORIZATION TO PREPAY CALPERS FY 2023­24 UNFUNDED
  ACCRUED LIABILITY (UAL) AMORTIZATION PAYMENTS
  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City prepay its FY 2023­24 UAL amortization payments to

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City prepay its FY 2023­24 UAL amortization payments to
  CalPERS for an estimated net savings of $51,997.32. If the City Council concurs
  with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be: “I move to authorize
  staff to prepay all of the City’s Fiscal Year 2023­24 unfunded accrued liability
  amortization payments to CalPERS in the total amount of $2,878,594, and to make
  such payments no later than July 31, 2023.”

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTION

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the City
received by members of the City Council. All public writings distributed by the City of San
Marino to at least a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be
made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San
Marino, California 91108, and will also be included in the public agenda packet that will
available for review at the City Council meeting.
